input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view (side-by-side) in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the core experiment-comparison capability in the Dashboard:
data scientists can select two or more training and pipeline runs and view
their parameters and metrics side by side. This removes the need to export run
data to spreadsheets when iterating on experiments and comparing candidate
runs for model promotion. The run diff view (highlighting changed parameters
and metrics between two runs) is a separate deferrable feature tracked in its
own epic; this epic delivers only the side-by-side comparison surface.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- Side-by-side view of parameters and metrics for all selected runs.
- Retrieval of run parameters and metrics through the existing Data Science
  Pipelines interfaces (KFP v2 API) — no Data Science Pipelines code changes
  are in scope for this work.
- Comparison stays within a single project; cross-cluster and cross-project
  comparison are out of scope, as is automatic best-run selection or promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing two or more runs, when the user selects them and
  opens the comparison, then the parameters and metrics of all selected runs
  are displayed side by side.
- The comparison works against runs produced by Data Science Pipelines using
  its existing run interfaces, with no Data Science Pipelines code changes
  (passive-component validation).
- Comparison is scoped to runs within a single project; no cross-project or
  cross-cluster comparison is offered.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard.

# Run lineage on registered model versions in the Model Registry

## Description

This epic makes registered model versions carry a reference to the run that
produced them, so that any consumer of the Model Registry can resolve the
training/pipeline lineage of a model version. It uses the Model Registry's
existing extension point for structured metadata on model versions (custom
properties), keeping the change within established registry patterns.

## Scope

- Capture a producing-run reference on registered model versions at
  registration time. The reference must be sufficient to resolve the run
  (project and run identity). Specific property naming and exact capture
  mechanism are implementation decisions for the Model Registry team within
  the custom-properties extension point.
- Ensure registration flows can supply the run reference, including
  registration performed from within a pipeline run.
- Expose the run reference on model versions through the Model Registry REST
  API so clients (such as the Dashboard) can read it.
- Registration flows that have no run reference continue to work; the lineage
  link is additive and optional.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a known run, the stored model version
  carries a reference that resolves to that run.
- The producing-run reference is readable through the Model Registry REST API
  on the model version entity.
- Existing registration flows without a run reference succeed unchanged
  (backwards compatible; the link is optional metadata).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, storage and exposure side): registered model versions link back
  to the run that produced them.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic surfaces run lineage in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI: a
registered model version shows the run that produced it, and the user can open
the run comparison view from there, seeded with that run. This connects model
promotion decisions to the underlying experiments without leaving the
platform.

This work depends on two capabilities being in place: the run comparison view
in the Dashboard (so there is a comparison to open and seed), and the
producing-run reference stored on registered model versions by the Model
Registry (so there is lineage to display).

## Scope

- Display the producing-run reference on registered model versions in the
  Dashboard's Model Registry UI.
- Provide an action from a model version to open the run comparison view
  seeded with its producing run, allowing the user to add further runs for
  side-by-side comparison.
- Graceful degradation: model versions without a producing-run reference show
  no lineage link and no errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a producing-run reference,
  the Model Registry UI in the Dashboard displays the run that produced it.
- Given such a model version, when the user opens the comparison from the
  registry, then the comparison view opens seeded with the producing run and
  the user can select additional runs to compare against.
- Given a model version with no producing-run reference, the registry page
  renders without a lineage link and without errors.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, UI side): a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic documents the new experiment-comparison workflow end to end, from
both entry points: selecting runs from the runs list in the Dashboard, and
opening a comparison from a registered model version's run lineage in the
Model Registry. It gives data scientists a single authoritative walkthrough
replacing the current exported-spreadsheet practice.

Documentation is authored after the implementation work it describes, so the
documented behavior matches what shipped.

## Scope

- A documentation topic (or topics) covering the comparison workflow:
  selecting two or more runs from the runs list, reading the side-by-side
  parameters/metrics view, and interpreting the diff highlighting between two
  runs.
- Coverage of the registry-driven path: opening a comparison from a registered
  model version via its producing-run link, including how a model version
  comes to carry a run reference.
- Screenshots and procedure steps consistent with the shipped UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers opening a comparison by selecting runs from the runs
  list, including the diff view between two runs.
- Documentation covers opening a comparison from the Model Registry via a
  model version's run lineage.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of
  the comparison view and the registry lineage integration before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.

# Run diff view in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the run "diff" view: when a user has selected two runs to
compare, the view highlights which parameters and metrics changed between
them, so data scientists can immediately see what differed between candidate
runs when making model promotion decisions. It is a deferrable enhancement to
the side-by-side run comparison capability: the side-by-side view is fully
usable without it.

This work depends on the side-by-side run comparison capability being in
place: the diff view is rendered within that comparison surface and reuses its
run selection and parameter/metric retrieval rather than building a second
surface. The shared surface is handled as a coordination gate on this epic,
not as a reason to fuse the two features into one priority.

## Scope

- Diff view that highlights which parameters and metrics differ between two
  selected runs, rendered within the existing run comparison surface.
- Reuse of the run comparison surface's multi-select and parameter/metric
  retrieval; no duplicate comparison surface or second data path is built
  (coordination gate with the side-by-side comparison work).
- Unchanged values are distinguishable from changed ones.
- Diff comparison stays within a single project, consistent with the
  side-by-side view's scoping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two selected runs, when the user opens the diff view, then parameters
  and metrics that changed between the two runs are highlighted, and unchanged
  values are distinguishable from changed ones.
- The diff view is rendered within the same comparison surface as the
  side-by-side view, reusing its run selection and parameter/metric retrieval;
  no second comparison surface or data path is introduced.
- The diff view operates on runs within a single project only, consistent with
  the side-by-side comparison scoping.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and
  metrics changed between two selected runs.

# Decomposition: RHAISTRAT-9015 — Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Major. Triage: not
below-threshold (spans three components and three owning teams), not docs-only
(substantive code changes in Dashboard and Model Registry).

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 | Run comparison view (side-by-side) in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E002 | Run lineage on registered model versions in the Model Registry | Implementation | Model Registry | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E003 | Open run comparison from the Model Registry in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E004 | Document the run comparison workflow | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E005 | Run diff view in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Run comparison view (P0)"] --> E003["E003 Registry-to-comparison entry (P1)"]
    E002["E002 Run lineage in Model Registry (P1)"] --> E003
    E001 --> E005["E005 Run diff view (P1)"]
    E001 --> E004["E004 Documentation (P1)"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
    E005 --> E004
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | The registry entry point launches and seeds the comparison view produced by the run comparison work; it builds against that UI capability, so it is serial. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact-producing → consuming) | The registry UI entry point renders the producing-run reference that the Model Registry lineage work stores on model versions; without that data artifact there is nothing to surface. |
| E001 → E005 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | The diff view is rendered within the comparison surface delivered by the side-by-side comparison work and reuses its run selection and parameter/metric retrieval, so it builds against that UI capability. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation must describe the comparison view as built. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation must describe the registry lineage behavior as built. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry, so it needs the registry entry point in place. |
| E005 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation covers interpreting the diff highlighting between two runs, so it needs the diff view in place. |
| No edge E001 ∥ E002 | Rule 14 (different repos, no shared artifacts) | Dashboard and Model Registry are separate repos with independent changes; they run in parallel and converge at E003. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epics | Coverage |
|-----|----------|-------|----------|
| HLR-1 (side-by-side comparison of 2+ runs in Dashboard) | P0 | E001 | Full |
| HLR-2 (registered model versions link back to producing run; comparison openable from registry) | P1 | E002 (lineage storage/exposure), E003 (registry UI entry) | Full |
| HLR-3 (run diff view highlighting changed parameters and metrics) | P1 | E005 | Full |
| HLR-4 (documentation of comparison workflow from runs list and registry) | P2 | E004 | Full |

All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Decomposition Notes

- **Component classification (Step 2)**: Dashboard and Model Registry are
  active components (code changes) and generate Implementation epics. Data
  Science Pipelines is classified **passive**: the comparison consumes run
  parameters and metrics through its existing KFP v2 REST API/SDK interfaces
  (architecture context: `rhoai-3.0/data-science-pipelines.md`), and the
  strategy identifies no DSP code change. Passive-component validation is an
  acceptance criterion on E001 ("comparison works against Data Science
  Pipelines runs via existing interfaces; no DSP code changes"). See Health
  Warnings for the residual ambiguity around registration-time run stamping.
- **All components are in the platform**: architecture context files exist for
  Dashboard, Model Registry, and Data Science Pipelines (all GA, Konflux
  onboarded). No repo/license/konflux onboarding chains apply. Documentation is
  a canonical Jira component (`.context/rhai-components.txt`) used for the
  docs-authoring epic; it is a content-process component, not a code component
  to provision, so Rule 20's onboarding chain does not apply to it.
- **Priority split decision (Step 4, revised)**: HLR-3 (P1, diff view) is split
  from HLR-1 (P0, side-by-side view) into its own epic E005. Although the diff
  view shares the same UI surface and the same parameter/metric data as the
  side-by-side view, HLR-3 is a distinct deferrable feature — a first-class
  requirement with its own HLR ID and acceptance criteria, delivering separate
  user value, and the P0 side-by-side capability is fully deliverable without
  it — so the independent-deferral planning requirement overrides the shared
  surface. The shared surface is handled as a coordination/AC gate on E005 (it
  must render within the existing comparison surface and reuse its selection
  and data retrieval rather than build a second surface), not as a reason to
  fuse the two priorities. HLR-2's Dashboard portion (E003) is likewise split
  from E001: it is a deferrable feature with independent user value (registry
  entry point) gated on another team's deliverable (E002), and it consumes —
  rather than rebuilds — the comparison view.
- **Priority inheritance**: E001 stays P0 (delivers HLR-1 directly). E002 is P1
  (enables HLR-2 only). E003 is P1 (HLR-2). E005 is P1 (HLR-3). E004 is a
  docs-authoring epic, exempt from priority inheritance; its P1 comes from the
  strategy frontmatter priority `Major` → P1 per the docs-authoring priority
  exception (not from HLR-4's P2 level).
- **Investigations**: the strategy declares "Open Questions: None" and
  contains no pending reviews, conditional ADRs, or risks table. No unknown
  meets the "changes which downstream epics exist" bar, so no Investigation
  epics were created. The one unclear passage (how the producing-run reference
  gets stamped at registration time) is an implementation detail resolvable by
  the Model Registry team within E002's scope, not a flagged genuine unknown.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
   Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, and no
   Non-Functional Requirements. Decomposition proceeded from the HLRs, Affected
   Components list, and Out-of-Scope list; epic acceptance criteria were
   derived accordingly. Owning teams were taken from architecture context.
2. **Data Science Pipelines scope ambiguity**: DSP is listed as an affected
   component, but no code change is identifiable from the strategy — classified
   passive (see Decomposition Notes). If capturing the producing-run reference
   at registration turns out to require pipeline-side/SDK changes in DSP (e.g.
   stamping run metadata when a pipeline registers a model), a follow-up DSP
   epic owned by RHOAI Pipelines may be needed; this should be confirmed when
   the Model Registry lineage work starts. Non-blocking.
3. **Documentation team inferred**: there is no architecture context file for
   the Documentation component; the canonical component name from
   `.context/rhai-components.txt` was used and the owning team was inferred as
   RHOAI Documentation. Verify assignment before creating the Jira epic.
4. **Docs priority vs HLR level**: E004 is P1 (docs-authoring exception maps
   strategy priority Major → P1) even though its source HLR-4 is P2. This is
   per-rule, not a priority inversion; flagged here so it is not read as one.
5. **Requirement wording overlap**: the problem statement notes requirements
   were consolidated from two customer councils with overlapping wording kept.
   No contradiction found between HLRs; no action needed.
6. **HLR-3 shared-surface coordination**: HLR-3 (P1, run diff view) is a
   separate epic (E005) so planners can defer it independently of the P0
   side-by-side work. Because both features share the same comparison UI
   surface and parameter/metric data, E005 carries a coordination gate: it must
   render within the comparison surface delivered by the P0 work and reuse its
   run selection and data retrieval rather than build a second surface. The
   two epics are owned by the same team (RHOAI Dashboard), which keeps that
   coordination internal.

decomposition_quality 3/5 — SCORE: 3

**The probed failure occurred (Dimension 2 — Epic boundaries: material gap).**

The dataset annotation defines this case as a redundancy-detection probe: HLR-1 ("select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side") and HLR-3 ("a diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs") describe the same Dashboard comparison surface in different words — the strategy itself signals this ("some overlap in wording was kept from the sources"). The expected handling is ONE comparison epic whose HLR Traceability lists both HLR-1 and HLR-3.

The decomposition instead produced two sibling epics — E001 (side-by-side view, HLR-1, P0) and E005 (diff view, HLR-3, P1) — both owned by RHOAI Dashboard, both building UI on the same comparison surface over the same run parameter/metric data. That is exactly the "two sibling epics each building a comparison/diff UI" scope-duplication failure this case probes.

Notably, the decomposition *detected* the overlap and declined to act on it: Health Warning 5 records the wording overlap and concludes "no action needed," and Health Warning 6, E005's coordination-gate AC, and the E001→E005 edge exist solely to patch the artificial boundary (forbidding a second surface/data path that a consolidated epic would never have risked creating). The split is rationalized on deferral grounds (P0 vs P1), but under the redundancy reading HLR-3 is a restatement of HLR-1, not a first-class separate feature — so the traceability matrix presents one capability as two, and the diff aspect of the P0 comparison capability is deferred into a P1 epic. The mitigations (dependency edge, anti-duplication AC, same-team ownership) reduce practical harm but do not undo the structural duplication. The internal adversarial review endorsed the split, but the annotation's ground truth for this probe is consolidation, and the rubric explicitly classes a boundary overlap as a material gap — especially where it is the single behavior the case was constructed to test.

**The other four dimensions are solid:**

- **HLR coverage (pass):** all four HLRs map to epic traceability sections; matrix present; priority inheritance correct (E001 is the P0 root; no lower-priority epic gates higher-priority work; E004 is docs-authoring and exempt, with its P1 derived per the stated exception).
- **DAG quality (pass):** diagram edges match every epic's frontmatter `dependencies` exactly; arrows run dependency→dependent; edges justified (framework→consumer for E001→E003/E005, genuine artifact edge E002→E003, Rule 11 docs-last into E004); E001∥E002 and E003∥E005 correctly parallel; no cycles. (The E001→E005 edge is well-formed given the split, though it exists only because of it.)
- **Scope fidelity (pass, one nit):** epic bodies reference siblings in plain capability terms, never draft IDs; no invented API paths, field names, or response formats. The "KFP v2 API" interface named in E001/E005 scope is not in the strategy and sits in tension with dashboard.md's "Kubernetes API only," but the load-bearing AC ("existing run interfaces, no DSP code changes") is interface-agnostic — a precision nit, not invented design. E002's custom-properties mechanism is architecture-context-validated with specifics explicitly deferred.
- **Acceptance criteria (pass):** three testable ACs per epic, traceable to the HLRs; docs technical-review AC present on E004; passive-component validation AC on E001; no replacement or konflux-onboarding work, so no rollback/build-pipeline ACs are required; out-of-scope constraints encoded as ACs rather than dropped.

**Calibration:** one material gap (the probed scope duplication) with everything else clean → 3. Not 2: there is no second material gap and no invented implementation detail (the KFP v2 naming is a nit; the review's ai-signals generosity findings fall outside these five dimensions). Not 4 or 5: the gap is the core of what this case tests — the decomposition's own artifacts show it saw the redundancy (Health Warnings 5–6) and chose to split anyway, and the rubric treats "two epics building the same UI surface" as a boundary overlap, i.e., material, not minor. | [informational] internal adversarial review score 13/14
